title: Say What You Know
paragraphs: Say what you know, but do not lecture. Listen well to what is said, but do not take it all for truth.
Just as silence does not mean you know nothing, talking much does not prove you know a great deal. To belittle a person is folly; to exalt them beyond measure is cowardice.
Speak rightly, listen rightly, and know how to be silent. Neither belittle a person nor lift them to the heavens—see them as they are.

title: The One Who Knows and the One Who Does Not
paragraphs: (A Chinese proverb)
He who does not know, and knows that he does not know—hungers for knowledge. Teach him!
He who knows, and does not know that he knows—is asleep. Awaken him!
He who does not know, and does not know that he does not know—is a fool. Keep away from him!
He who knows, and knows that he knows—is a leader. Follow him!
Teach the one who hungers to learn; awaken the one lost in heedlessness; keep away from the fool who imagines he knows everything; and follow the one who truly knows.

title: The Tongue
paragraphs: The tongue is a flower that grows in the mouth;
if you do not water and tend it, it withers and is lost.
If the tongue is not guarded, it fades like a flower left unwatered. To keep the mother tongue alive is to use it every day with love.

title: What Is a Word
paragraphs: There is a word that wounds;
there is a word that is a pearl.
A word can be a thorn that wounds, or a precious pearl. What makes the difference is how you use it.

title: Word and Silence
paragraphs: Sometimes a person says more by remaining silent. For a word is not merely sound—it is the mirror of intention.
If a word will break a heart, if a sentence will extinguish hope—it is not worth saying.
If the word you would speak will not warm a heart, will not bring a smile—be silent.
Remember… not every word opens into a flower. Some are like thorns—they wound whoever they touch.
Silence is wisdom. And sometimes it is the most precious answer.
If a word is born of the heart, it becomes wisdom; if it flies from a thoughtless mouth, it becomes harm and leaves a wound.
Be silent. For silence, too, speaks—sometimes more deeply, sometimes more honestly.
Not every word opens into a flower; some wound like thorns. In place of a word that will bring no good, silence is the wiser choice.

title: Saying the Word in Its Place
paragraphs: One who knows how to say the word in its place need never be forced to apologize.
One who speaks the word in its place need never afterward be forced to ask forgiveness. The right word is precious at the right moment.

title: Silence
paragraphs: The answer to some questions is silence.
Either it is not the time for an answer,
or the one you speak with is not worthy of one!
Dervish Jalal Ruhevi
The truest answer to some questions is silence—either it is not the time, or the one before you is not worthy of a reply.

title: The Silent Corridor
paragraphs: There were two organizations working together—one a sponsor, the other a body that prepared projects.

For months the project team labored with great care, polishing the documents meticulously, and one day, when everything was ready, they sent the materials to the sponsor and began to wait for a reply. Days passed, weeks passed. The result—silence.
Within the team, uncertainty grew and spread like a shadow stretching the length of a corridor:
«Did the documents arrive? Have they been looked at?»
No one had clear information. Approaches to the sponsor brought only veiled, vague answers.
Several months later the team decided to go straight to the sponsor’s office to settle the matter. There, at last, the truth came to light:
«Yes, the documents arrived. But we did not accept them. Because the form of presentation was incorrect and the official procedure was not followed.»
The team stood frozen on the spot.
«Then why did you not tell us?» — they asked.
«We could have put everything right in a short time.»…
Returning to their office in disappointment, the staff remonstrated with their own leadership:

«If we had followed the process actively, checked the status regularly, and built clear communication, this misunderstanding would never have happened. We lost our time, spent our energy in vain, and our trust was shaken—all because the corridor between us remained silent.»

When communication is unclear, even the finest work may go unseen. Without follow-up, even the strongest partnership may weaken. In collaboration the greatest enemy is often not failure—it is silence.

title: The Shepherd Must Be Called
paragraphs: A student who wished to complete the education he had received over long years went to his master to seek his blessing.
His master said:

— Very well, but I have one condition. I will ask you a question, to see whether in these years you have properly learned the knowledge I gave you. If you answer correctly, I will know my labor was not in vain, and I will give you my blessing.
The student, sure of himself, said:
— Please, master, ask.
His master said:
— My child, imagine you are going to your village and on the way a shepherd’s pack of rabid dogs attacks you. You face danger. What would you do to save your life?
— I would bend down, pick up a few stones from the ground, throw them at the dogs, and drive them off.
— But, my child, you throw a stone at one, you throw at two—you cannot deal with them all. They will join forces and tear you apart.
— Then I would turn and run.
— Be sure of this: they run faster than you; they will catch you. What then?
The student saw that he was at a loss and asked his master for help.
His master said:
— My child, there is only one way out of this plight: you must call the shepherd and ask him to hold his dogs. The moment the dogs hear the shepherd’s voice, they will freeze where they stand.
Not every problem is solved by force. Sometimes stepping back and looking differently is the shortest way out.

title: The Shepherd’s Word
paragraphs: Once in a village there lived a poor but honest shepherd named Hasan. One day the village lord summoned him and said:
— O Hasan, I have heard that you know the mountain pastures well. This summer I entrust my flock to you. If in autumn my animals return healthy and fat, I will give you a cow as a gift.

Hasan agreed. All summer, rain or shine, he grazed the flock and watched over it night after night without closing his eyes. When autumn came, the flock returned to the village fatter and healthier than before.
Hoping to receive the promised cow, Hasan went to the lord. But the lord smiled with scorn and said:
— I never meant to give you a cow; those words were only to spur you to the work. You are poor as it is—what would you do with a cow?
Hasan’s eyes filled with tears. Yet he answered calmly and with dignity:
— You are right, my lord: I am poor. But I have a conscience, and I am master of my own word. You may be rich, yet if the word you give is worth nothing, then the truly poor one is you.

These words passed from mouth to mouth in the village. The lord’s name fell from honor, and people began to avoid doing business with him. And he, though late, came to understand: a person’s worth is determined not by wealth or rank, but by fidelity to his word.
A person’s true wealth is not property, but his word, his conscience, and his trustworthiness.

title: Communication
paragraphs: If you often keep company with the elderly and with children, in the one you will see experience, and in the other, purity.
From the old one learns experience; from the child, purity. Every age has a value it can give a person.

title: The Candles’ Conversation
paragraphs: In a room four candles burned softly. The place was so quiet that one could hear the candles talking among themselves.
The first candle said: «I am FAITH! But no one helps me burn. It seems I shall soon go out.»
And so it was. Its flame began to dwindle swiftly, and at last FAITH went out completely.
The second candle: «I am LOYALTY! Alas, I am no longer needed by anyone. And so there is no longer any meaning in my burning.»
Hardly had it finished speaking when a light breeze blew and extinguished LOYALTY as well.

Then came the third candle’s turn. In a sorrowful voice it said: «I am LOVE! I have no strength left to burn. People have forgotten me; my worth has vanished. Even those closest to them have forgotten how to love.»
LOVE, too, could bear it no longer and went out.
At that moment a child entered the room and saw that none of the three candles was burning. «Why are you not burning? Were you not meant to burn forever?» he said, and began to weep.
Then the fourth candle spoke: «Do not be afraid; so long as I burn, we can light the others again. I am HOPE!»
The child rejoiced, took the HOPE candle in his hand with shining eyes, and lit the other candles one by one.
When faith, loyalty, and love go out, it is hope that lights them again. If we keep the light of hope, the other values will rise anew as well.
